name: Nimble Lead to Cash
author: nimbleplugins.com

sections.description:
Lead to Cash by NimblePlugins is a self-hosted workflow for service businesses that want to manage the path from enquiry to invoice inside WordPress.

Most small service businesses run on a contact form, a spreadsheet, a folder of PDF files and an accounting program that first hears about a job once it is over. Lead to Cash replaces the middle of that chain. An enquiry arrives, becomes a quote, the quote becomes a job, the job becomes an invoice, and the invoice is followed until it is paid – in one place, on your own server, with the history of every step kept beside the record it belongs to.

It is not a set of custom post types with an admin screen in front. Lead to Cash creates its own database tables and runs as a private single-page app on your site, opened from the WordPress admin menu and reachable only by the users you give access to. The working day happens in that app; the WordPress admin is where you configure it.

From enquiry to paid invoice

Enquiries. New enquiries are listed as they arrive, with the source they came from, the owner responsible, the status, and the next action with a date on it. Actions whose date has passed are raised on the dashboard before you start, so nothing waits quietly. Enquiries that come in by phone are written straight into the same list, and a second enquiry on a contact who already has one open is flagged before it is saved.

Customers. Each contact has a single record: details, the enquiries behind them, their documents, what they currently owe, and the activity history beside it. A Danish CVR number or a European VAT number can be looked up, so the registered name and address are filled in for you.

Quotes. A quote is written with line items, an introduction and your own terms attached, produced as a PDF and emailed to the customer from the site. Every quote carries its value and its expiry date, so the pipeline shows what is genuinely still open rather than everything ever sent.

Jobs. An accepted quote becomes a job with an owner, a deadline, a priority and an economy of its own. Finished work moves to a completed list that stays searchable, with the invoices raised against it linked from the job.

Invoices. Invoices are produced as PDF documents with your payment terms and, if you use one, a payment QR code. An invoice runs from draft to paid and keeps track of partial payments, credit notes and what is overdue – and it remembers which job it came from.

Reports and audit log. The reports cover enquiries received, win rate, what was quoted, what was invoiced, what was paid, and how long payment actually took. The audit log records every change: who made it, when, and what it touched.

What the free plugin includes

  • Enquiries and manual lead creation
  • Customers
  • Quotes and PDF documents
  • Jobs and completed work
  • Invoices and payment tracking
  • Standard reports and an audit log
  • In-app notifications
  • Search and export tools
  • Local encryption of sensitive fields
  • WordPress personal-data export and erasure integration
  • English as the default product language
  • Danish language and economic defaults
  • A searchable Help & FAQ centre in English and Danish
  • Lead to Cash user administration in WordPress
  • Scheduled backups of Lead to Cash data, kept on the server, with restore and import of a saved backup file

Users and access

Whether a person may open Lead to Cash at all is a WordPress capability, carried by a dedicated “Lead to Cash operator” role that the plugin adds. What they may do once inside is a separate setting with three levels – User, Consultant and Admin – so an administrator of the website is not automatically an administrator of the business data. Both are managed from the WordPress admin.

Your data stays on your server

Lead to Cash stores everything in its own tables in your WordPress database, and keeps its backups there as well. Sensitive contact and activity fields are encrypted locally with an installation key that is never sent anywhere, and you can define that key in wp-config.php so that a copy of the database on its own cannot decrypt your customer data.

The plugin never contacts NimblePlugins, sends no analytics and has no telemetry. It reaches the internet only when a user asks for something that needs it – a CVR or VAT lookup, or a logo or QR image given as a web address. Each case is listed under External services below.

It also plugs into WordPress’s own Export Personal Data and Erase Personal Data tools, and it can remove every trace of itself on uninstall if you turn that option on.

English and Danish

English is the product language. Danish is translated throughout, and choosing it also switches the economic defaults: DKK, 25% VAT, CVR labels and Danish document prefixes. Documents that are already saved keep the values they were written with. A searchable Help & FAQ centre is built in, in both languages.

No licence, no account, no time limit

The free plugin is complete on its own. There is no licence check, no account requirement, no feature that expires and no upsell in the middle of the workflow. A product key applies only to the separately installed Lead to Cash Pro add-on, whose code is not part of this plugin.

Product information: https://nimbleplugins.com/lead-to-cash/

External services

Lead to Cash runs on your own server and never contacts NimblePlugins. It contacts the services below, and only for the feature named.

Danish company register, CVR (only when a user looks up a CVR number)

When a user enters a Danish CVR number on a customer card and asks for the details, the eight-digit number is sent to cvrapi.dk to fetch the registered company name and address. The request also carries this site’s host name in the User-Agent header, because cvrapi.dk rejects anonymous calls. Nothing else is sent, and no customer data leaves the site. An answer is cached for twelve hours, so looking the same number up again does not call out again.

Service: https://cvrapi.dk/ – Terms: https://cvrapi.dk/terms – What data they hold and why: https://cvrapi.dk/help

VAT-number lookup (only when a user clicks it)

When a user looks up a customer’s VAT number, the country code and the number are sent to the European Commission’s VIES service (ec.europa.eu) to fetch the registered company name and address. Nothing else is sent. Service: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/ – Legal notice: https://commission.europa.eu/legal-notice_en – Privacy: https://commission.europa.eu/privacy-policy-websites-managed-european-commission_en

Logo and payment QR image

If the company logo or payment QR code is given as a web address, Lead to Cash downloads that image to place it in PDF documents. Only the address you enter is requested, and nothing about your data is sent. Normally this is an image in your own media library.

Backup destinations (only with the separate Pro add-on)

Lead to Cash takes backups and keeps them on this server. Sending a copy somewhere else is what Pro adds: Pro registers the destinations, and without Pro there are none, so a backup stays where it was made.

This package does contain the Dropbox client class, because Pro builds on it rather than carrying its own copy. It is never reached without Pro: every path to it runs through a destination, and no destination exists until Pro registers one.

With Pro installed and a destination configured, the backup archive is uploaded to the destination you chose, each time a backup runs. The archive contains all Lead to Cash data, so choose a destination you would trust with the database itself.

Dropbox: https://www.dropbox.com/ – Terms: https://www.dropbox.com/terms – Privacy: https://www.dropbox.com/privacy

Google Drive: https://www.google.com/drive/ – Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms – Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

OneDrive and SharePoint: https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/onedrive – Terms: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement – Privacy: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/privacy/privacystatement

SFTP and webhook destinations go to an address you enter yourself; no third party is involved beyond the one you choose.

Source code

Lead to Cash has no build step. The JavaScript and CSS shipped in frontend/ and admin/ are the source: written by hand, not generated, bundled or minified, and they are the same files the browser loads. There is nothing to un-minify, and there are no build tools to document.

Privacy

Lead to Cash stores contact details, enquiry details, notes, document data and activity history in the local WordPress database. Sensitive fields are encrypted locally.

The plugin integrates with WordPress personal-data export and erasure tools. Site administrators remain responsible for defining suitable retention periods. Financial records may need to be retained under applicable bookkeeping rules.

Lead to Cash does not contact NimblePlugins. Backups sent to a destination contain all Lead to Cash data; choose a destination you would trust with the database itself.

readme.txt carries only the most recent entries, because the plugin
directory truncates that section at 5000 characters. Everything is here.

1.37.29

  • Tabellen til udgaaende beskeder bliver nu faktisk oprettet naar en
    eksisterende installation opdaterer. Tabellen kom med i 1.37.28, men
    skemaversionen blev staaende paa 0.9.2, og opgraderingen koerer kun
    skematrinnet naar den vaerdi aendrer sig. En ny installation fik tabellen,
    en opdateret gjorde ikke – og fejlen kunne kun ses paa et site der havde
    pluginnet i forvejen.

1.37.28

  • Henvendelser tælles nu på hvornår de kom ind, ikke på hvornår de blev
    skrevet ned. En henvendelse fra juli, der først tastes ind i oktober,
    hørte til oktober i rapporten – så juli mistede den, og oktober fik en
    for meget. Feltet “Modtaget” på henvendelsen afgør det, og rapporten,
    ugetællingen og begge lister regner nu på det samme.

1.37.25

  • Gennemført én regel i rapporten: det realiserede vinder altid. Er der
    først en faktura på en opgave eller en henvendelse, ER fakturaen værdien,
    og budgettet eller det aftalte beløb tæller ikke med nogen steder – hverken
    som rest eller som et højere tal.
  • Restbeløbet på delvist fakturerede opgaver er fjernet helt.
  • “Gns. hvor værdien er kendt” tog før det største af det fakturerede og det
    aftalte. Et budget, ingen nogensinde fakturerede, kunne dermed slå den
    faktura, der afsluttede sagen. Nu er det fakturaen, når der er en.
  • “Aftalt, endnu ikke faktureret” dækker nu kun sager helt uden faktura.

1.37.24

  • Noterne under Samlet opgaveværdi er fjernet. Opdelingen står allerede på
    siden, og tre linjer under et tal gør kortet sværere at læse, ikke lettere.

1.37.23

  • Henvendelsesraten talte forud. Med en periode, der løb til 31. december,
    blev november og december regnet med som stille måneder, og raten blev
    delt med tid, der ikke var gået: 48 henvendelser blev til 9,1 om måneden
    i stedet for 18,7. Den regner nu frem til i dag, som ugelisten altid har
    gjort.

1.37.22

  • Rapporter målte værdi på henvendelser. En henvendelse er ikke en værdi, og
    en kunde er det heller ikke – værdien opstår først, når nogen skriver ned,
    hvad en opgave koster. Kortet hedder nu “Samlet opgaveværdi” og er det
    fakturerede plus budgettet på de opgaver, der endnu ikke er faktureret.
  • Er en opgave budgetteret højere, end den er faktureret, står forskellen
    frem som aftalt, ikke endnu faktureret arbejde. Før forsvandt den helt.
  • Rapportperioden starter som hele indeværende år, 1. januar til 31. december,
    i stedet for et vindue, der gled en dag frem hver morgen.

1.37.21

  • Statusfilteret “Alle” på opgavelisten skjulte de afsluttede. Det modsagde sit
    eget navn, og en afsluttet opgave kunne kun ses i den separate
    Afsluttede-visning. “Alle” betyder nu alle.
  • “Planlagt” er valgt som standard, for det er den liste, man handler på.

1.37.20

  • Opgaver kunne blive til tvillinger. Gemmestien afgjorde opret-eller-opdatér
    ud fra et data-attribut på formularen, som blev nulstillet, hver gang
    dialogen blev lukket. En formular, der havde mistet sit id, oprettede derfor
    en ny opgave i stedet for at gemme den, der stod på skærmen. Identiteten
    læses nu af selve posten; attributtet er kun et krydstjek.
  • Opretter du en opgave på en kunde, der allerede har en åben, viser appen de
    eksisterende og spørger, før den opretter. Serveren afviser en ubekræftet
    dublet og sender de åbne opgaver med tilbage, så spørgsmålet kan nævne dem.
    Det er et spørgsmål, ikke et forbud — to åbne opgaver på samme kunde er ofte
    rigtigt.
  • Nøgletallet på opgavelisten var ét tal, der lagde fakturerede beløb sammen
    med håndtastede budgetter, og som talte alle opgaver med — også de
    afsluttede, tabellen ikke viser. Samme arbejde kunne derfor tælle to gange:
    én gang som omsætning på den afsluttede opgave, én gang som forventning på
    tvillingen. Det er nu to tal — Faktureret og Forventet — og begge følger det,
    der står i listen, så filter og søgning virker på dem.
  • Økonomikolonnen blandede momsgrundlag: fakturerede opgaver viste beløb
    inklusive moms, resten viste budget uden. Alt vises nu ekskl. moms, og det
    står i kolonneoverskriften.

1.37.19

  • Appens adresse kan nu vælges. Har sitet allerede en side på /lead-to-cash/ —
    en produktside, en landingsside — nægtede pluginnet at blive aktiveret, og
    eneste udvej var at omdøbe den eksisterende side. Det er ikke rimeligt at
    forlange af et site, der havde adressen først. Sæt
    define( ‘NIMBLE_LTC_APP_SLUG’, ‘din-slug’ ); i wp-config.php før
    aktivering, så bruger appen den i stedet. Pro henter PWA’ens id, start_url,
    scope og Service-Worker-Allowed fra samme konstant, så det følger med.
  • Fejlbeskeden ved adressekonflikt sagde ikke, hvad man skulle gøre, og skrev
    altid “/lead-to-cash/” selv hvis appen lå et andet sted. Den viser nu den
    rigtige adresse og nævner konstanten.
  • Bemærk: ændrer man adressen på en eksisterende installation, skal
    permalinks gemmes igen, og PWA’en skifter scope, så genveje må tilføjes
    forfra.

1.37.18

  • Kundekortets overskrift stacker nu ordentligt på telefon. Henvisningen “Også
    kunde som …” klemte sig ind ved siden af navnet, wrappede over tre linjer og
    maste lukkekrydset. Navn og kryds beholder den første række, og henvisningen
    får en række for sig selv nedenunder. Et langt kundenavn kan ikke længere
    vokse chippen — den afkortes med ellipse.

1.37.17

  • Henvisningen “Også kunde som …” flugter nu med kundens navn i kortets
    overskrift, og den er endelig guld. Farverne gik før gennem en kæde af
    CSS-variabler inde i color-mix(); brister et led i den kæde, bliver
    variablen ugyldig, teksten arver hvid og baggrunden falder tilbage til den
    almindelige knapstil — præcis den blå, den ikke måtte være. Farverne står nu
    direkte, med en mørk guld til lyst tema og en lys til mørkt.

1.37.16

  • Henvisningen “Også kunde som …” er flyttet helt op i kortets egen overskrift,
    ved siden af kundens navn, og er nu guld. Guld bruges ikke andre steder i
    produktet, så den kan hverken forveksles med de blå handlingsknapper eller
    med noget andet. På smalle skærme falder den ned på sin …
sections.installation:
1. Install the ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or upload the nimble-lead-to-cash folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Lead to Cash by NimblePlugins.
  3. Open Lead to Cash in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Configure language and company settings.
  5. Open the private Lead to Cash app from the admin menu.
sections.faq:
Is Pro required?

No. The workflow for enquiries, customers, quotes, jobs, invoices, reports and exports is complete on its own.

Where is customer data stored?

In dedicated tables in the site’s WordPress database. Sensitive contact and activity fields are encrypted with a local installation key.

Does the Free plugin send telemetry?

No. Lead to Cash sends no analytics or telemetry.

Where is the encryption key stored?

Sensitive fields are encrypted locally with a key that is never sent anywhere. The key is read from the constant NIMBLE_LTC_ENCRYPTION_KEY_B64 in wp-config.php if you define one, and otherwise from an option in the database.

Defining it in wp-config.php is recommended. It keeps the key out of the database, so a database copy on its own — a support export, a shared dump, or a vulnerability in another plugin — cannot decrypt your customer data. Lead to Cash > Overview shows the exact line to add and can remove the database copy once it is in place.

Does the plugin contact an external service?

Only when you use a feature that needs one: the VAT-number lookup, or a logo or QR image you point at by web address. Nothing is sent to NimblePlugins, and nothing is sent at all until a user asks for it. Backups stay on this server. See External services for the details.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

Data is preserved. Deactivation does not remove customer or pipeline data.

Can I delete all plugin data on uninstall?

Yes. This is opt-in under Lead to Cash settings. If enabled before uninstalling Free, plugin-owned database tables, settings, private storage, local backups and the encryption key are removed. Leave the option disabled to preserve records.

Can I export or erase personal data?

Yes. The plugin integrates with WordPress Tools > Export Personal Data and Erase Personal Data.

What changes when Danish is selected?

New documents use Danish defaults such as DKK, 25% VAT, CVR labels and Danish document prefixes. Existing saved documents keep their historical values.
sections.changelog:
1.37.85

  • Time logged on a job that you have not seen yet is now marked in green: the
    row in the job list, and inside the job the visit that carries the time. It
    is the same kind of mark as the blue one for an unseen row, and it is read
    the same way – here is something new. Opening the job clears the mark for
    that job alone; the other jobs keep theirs, because a visit is only seen by
    someone who opened the job it sits on. Registrations older than thirty days
    do not light up.

1.37.84

  • The bell can now be narrowed to your own work. An administrator receives the
    work items for everyone – enquiries, quotes, jobs and invoices – so nothing
    goes unnoticed while a colleague is away. Where a single colleague owns every
    record, that is the whole list twice over, and the wide view can now be turned
    off per administrator. Operational failures and plugin updates stay with the
    administrator either way: they are the only ones who can act on them. The
    switch sits on the profile screen, which belongs to the Pro add-on; on its own
    the free plugin keeps the full view.

1.37.83

  • The plugin page now describes the work instead of listing feature names: how
    an enquiry becomes a quote, a job and an invoice, where the data is kept, who
    can reach it, and what the free plugin covers on its own. No code changed.

1.37.82

  • A notification added by an add-on can now be dismissed, as the filter’s own
    documentation has always promised. The key guard demanded exactly 64 hex
    characters – the shape of this plugin’s own sha256 keys – and silently
    discarded every other, so the button did nothing and there was nothing to
    look for.

1.37.81

  • A file the system produces itself can now be filed against both the contact
    and the enquiry, as an uploaded file always could. And it is called a
    contact, not a customer: a quote usually goes to an enquiry that has not
    become a customer yet.

1.37.80

  • A quote can now carry its own short message to the customer. It belongs on
    the quote rather than on the send: the moment of writing it is when you
    know what the files are, and it is the same sentence that should go along
    if the quote is sent again.

1.37.79

  • A quote now records which of two kinds it is: one with a generated
    document, or one that is the attached files themselves. The choice belongs
    on the quote rather than on the send, because it decides which fields there
    is any point filling in at all.

1.37.78

  • The company settings can now hold several named messages to send a quote
    with, not only one default. The default stays where it is and is still used
    when nothing else is chosen.
  • The document store has gained a path for files the system produces itself,
    such as a reply read from the mailbox and kept as it arrived. Deliberately
    separate from the upload route: that route’s list of accepted file types is
    a security boundary for what a user may hand over, and it should not be
    widened merely so the plugin can save something of its own.

1.37.77

  • An enquiry’s record now shows where it came from: the campaign and the
    landing page the visit started on. Both have been stored all along – the
    campaign in its own column, the full address in the enquiry’s details – but
    neither was ever displayed, so there was no way to see which ad paid for an
    enquiry without digging through the form log.
  • When the campaign field is empty, the campaign id is read from the landing
    page address instead. Google auto-tagging sends gclid and gad_campaignid,
    not utm_campaign, so for paid Google traffic the field stayed empty even
    though the id sat right beside it in the address. The line says plainly when
    the id was read from the address rather than written by someone.

1.37.76

  • Overview now shows “Won value this month” in place of “Invoice drafts”. The
    figure comes from the report’s own calculation — the same ladder: invoice,
    else quote, else job budget, else estimate — read from one place, so
    Overview and Reports cannot end up stating different amounts under the same
    word.
  • The card can be clicked and shows each won enquiry with the amount it
    contributes and where that amount comes from — invoice, quote, job budget
    or estimate. The rows are added up and checked against the total, so they
    cannot disagree. A row opens its own enquiry.

1.37.74

  • “Add inspection” did nothing on a job that had not been saved yet. An
    inspection belongs to a job that exists, so the button hit an early return
    with no error and no message, and looked dead. It now saves the job first
    and opens the inspection afterwards, exactly as “Create invoice” in the
    same dialog has always done.
  • The inspection dialog had no side padding — the fields sat flush against
    the edge — and was 1180px wide for seven fields. It now has padding and a
    width that fits what is in it.

1.37.72

  • The duplicate warning on a hand-entered enquiry now also covers a contact who
    is not a customer yet. It only looked for an established customer before, so
    two identical enquiries on the same prospect could go in a day apart with
    nobody asked – and the duplicate only surfaced when the won enquiries were
    counted and the name appeared twice.
  • The warning now says what it found. A contact with an enquiry under way is not
    “already a customer”, and a message that does not fit gets clicked past
    unread.
  • A contact whose enquiries are all lost or not relevant still raises no warning.
    That is new work, and a confirmation you always see catches nothing.

1.37.71

  • The twelve key figures on Overview can now be clicked too. The cards keep
    their shape, the order can still be dragged, and a click on the drag handle
    opens nothing. Overview deliberately does not load the large lists, so the
    rows are fetched on the click and the dialog opens straight away.
  • Where a card carries an amount, the rows are added up and compared with the
    figure. If they disagree, the dialog says so instead of looking right.
  • The summary cards on Enquiries, Jobs and Invoices can now be clicked, as
    Customers could in the previous version. Each card opens a dialog with the
    population, the arithmetic and the rows behind it, and a row opens its own
    record.
  • Each card now states what it was counted over. On Jobs the four status
    counts cover every job while Invoiced and Expected follow the filter and
    search on screen – two populations in the same row of cards. That was not
    written anywhere before.
  • On Invoices the counts come from the server and the amounts from the whole
    invoice book, a customer kept out of the figures included. That is why
    Invoices and Customers show different amounts, and every single invoice can
    now be pointed at in the dialog.
  • The “Credit notes” card has been removed from Invoices. “Credited” says the
    same thing about the same correction. The status filter still offers both,
    where they are two different lists.
  • A clickable card, and the rows inside a dialog, were drawn as action
    buttons. They now use the card surface.

1.37.68

  • The summary cards on Customers can be clicked. Each one opens a dialog that
    says what the figure is made of: the population it was counted over, how the
    amount is composed, and the rows behind it. A row opens its own record.
  • “Total customer value” now shows its own arithmetic – invoiced plus job
    budget plus estimate – and says so out loud if the parts do not add up.
  • “Customers” counts every contact while the money cards count only those in
    the figures. That difference was always there but could not be seen. The
    population is now stated on each card.
  • The four other overviews follow.

1.37.67

  • A job is now marked when its deadline is within a day, not only once it has
    passed. A deadline tomorrow morning is the one that can still be met; once
    it has gone by, the damage is done and the mark came too late.
  • Overdue and due-within-24-hours share one mark. Both ask something of you
    today, and two kinds of mark would only have to be learned by heart. The
    menu badge now says what it counts.
  • “Overdue” on the job list still counts only what has passed. The two answer
    different questions.

1.37.66

  • The Clear button from 1.37.65 now covers every optional date field, not just
    a job’s deadline: a quote’s “Valid until”, a recurrence’s “Repeat until”, a
    visit’s “Planned” and “Carried out”, an enquiry’s “Received”, and the
    MobilePay filter’s from-date. The same trap sat on all of them.
  • Fields that must have a value – invoice date, quote date, due date, start
    and end – get no button.
  • Why it matters in each place: a quote with the wrong “Valid until” reads as
    expired for good, and an enquiry with the wrong “Received” is counted in the
    wrong month – “Received” is the date every weekly and monthly figure is
    built on.

1.37.65

  • A job’s deadline can be cleared again. A Clear button now sits beside the
    field whenever a deadline is set. The back end could always do it – an empty
    field means no deadline – but a datetime-local can only be emptied from the
    keyboard, and on a phone it opens a picker with no clear. A deadline set by
    accident could only be moved, never removed.
  • That is not a small thing: the job is marked overdue and counted in the menu
    badge until the deadline passes – and a deadline set by accident has already
    passed, so the mark never went out.

1.37.64

  • The VAT hint wrote the amount with two full stops – “2,765.00 kr..” –
    because the amount already ends in “kr.” and the sentence added one more.

1.37.63

  • A job’s budget field now shows, as you type, what the amount comes to
    including VAT. The field is labelled “Expected revenue (excl. VAT)”, but a
    quote states both figures side by side and the inclusive one can end up
    there. The mirror line shows the figure you did not type, so the mistake
    catches itself at once.
  • When the amount ends in .25, .50 or .75 and divides evenly by the VAT rate,
    it is said out loud with a button that corrects it. Round numbers cannot be
    told apart – 20,000 can be either – so this is a hint and not a block.
  • A budget with VAT in it stands 25 per cent too high in total customer value,
    and on an open job the larger of budget and invoiced counts, so the wrong
    figure wins.

1.37.62

  • An active customer with no job at all can now be seen in the list. There is
    nothing to put the work on and nothing to budget, and an invoice can only be
    written straight on the customer – where neither the job list nor its figures
    will ever see it. Free marks the row; Pro, which has a job column, shows the
    zero in red inside white brackets.
  • And opening such a customer’s record asks whether a job should be created. A
    yes goes straight on to the job form with the customer filled in. It asks
    once per customer per session, not every time the record is opened.

1.37.61

  • A part payment written directly on a job that is still running was counted
    twice, once as revenue and once as expectation. A job with a 20,000 budget
    and 16,000 invoiced read as 36,000. The offset only counted documents with no
    job on them; it now counts documents on an open job as well.
  • Documents on a completed or cancelled job still do not offset anything. They
    paid for that job, and a closed job is worth only its invoice – letting them
    offset would eat another, open budget on the same enquiry.
  • The fault arrived in 1.37.59 with the new value rule and could only affect an
    open job that had an invoice on it.

1.37.60

  • The customer list scrolled sideways. Phone and email now sit under the name
    instead of in a column of their own, so a whole row fits without pushing it
    about. The table needed 1545 px and had 1402.
  • The “Value per won enquiry” card said “no invoice, quote or budget” about
    eleven enquiries – but two of them had an estimate written on them, and that
    estimate shows its amount on the customer list and counts towards total
    customer value. Those two now have a tile of their own, “Estimate only”, so
    the number reads nine. The two categories sum to the old one.

1.37.59

  • The customer list now shows what a customer is worth in total: what has been
    invoiced plus what is still waiting. There is a “Total” column per customer
    and a total row underneath, and that row does not follow the filter – every
    customer counted in the figures is in it, whoever you are looking at. The
    estimated amount is split by where it comes from: job budget and the estimate
    written on the enquiry, each on its own.
  • What counts as uninvoiced value now follows one rule, the same everywhere. A
    completed job is worth only its invoice; an open job the larger of its budget
    and what has been invoiced; a cancelled job nothing. Where the enquiry has no
    job at all, its estimate follows the same rule. A completed customer counts
    only what has been invoiced.
  • Before, an open job’s budget disappeared entirely as soon as a single invoice
    touched the enquiry – even when that invoice was for something else – and an
    invoice written on the enquiry could have the same work counted both as
    revenue and as expectation. The report’s job value and the customer list
    could not be reconciled with each other.
  • Four things are no longer possible: creating an invoice from an enquiry,
    adding a job to a completed customer, invoicing a completed job, and
    completing a customer that still has open jobs. The last three ask you to
    reopen the customer or the job first, and say so. Completing a customer with
    open jobs used to be a question you could answer yes to.
  • The job list’s “Expected” no longer counts the budget on a cancelled job.

1.37.58

  • An unread notification now shows in the browser tab itself. The bell inside
    the app can only be read while you are looking at the app, and a message is
    worth the most when you are doing something else. The tab title now carries
    the count – “(2) Lead to Cash” – and the tab icon carries a red badge with
    the same number.
  • When the app is installed on the machine, the application icon’s own badge
    is set as well. All three follow the same number as the bell, and they fail
    independently: if the icon cannot be redrawn, the count still stands in the
    title.
  • The app stopped asking for notifications as soon as the tab was hidden. That
    is exactly the case the badge exists for, so it keeps asking now.

1.37.57

  • Et tal i menuen peger nu paa sine egne raekker. Henvendelser, Kunder,
    Opgaver, Fakturaer og Afsluttede kan alle vise et tal, men det sagde kun hvor
    mange – ikke hvilke, og den ene opgave bag et 1-tal skulle findes i hovedet.
    De raekker, tallet er talt paa, faar nu en blaa markering i listen.
  • Markeringen kommer fra serveren sammen med tallet, saa badgen og listen ikke
    kan blive uenige: det er de samme raekker begge veje. Aabner man et afsnit,
    hvor tallet slukkes ved at se det – Kunder og Afsluttede – bliver markeringen
    staaende besoeget ud, saa man naar at se hvad der var nyt.
  • Tallet ved Kunder taeller nu kunder i stedet for vundne henvendelser. Vandt
    en kunde to henvendelser siden sidst, sagde det to om en liste, der kun havde
    en enkelt raekke at vise for det.

1.37.56

  • En afsluttet kunde uden nogen oekonomi er nu maerket i kundelisten. Det er
    seks nuller i traek – ingen opgave, ingen faktura, intet faktureret, intet
    anslaaet, intet udestaaende – som ellers skulle laegges sammen i hovedet for
    hver raekke. Den er enten aldrig blevet til noget eller lukket for tidligt,
    og begge dele er vaerd at faa oeje paa.
  • En sletning er markeret med roedt i loggen. Resultatfeltet siger kun om
    handlingen lykkedes, ikke hvor meget den fjernede, saa en vellykket sletning
    saa ud som enhver anden linje. Det gaelder enhver sletning, ikke kun kunder:
    det er handlingen, der ikke kan fortrydes.

1.37.55

  • Adressen en faktura sendes til kan rettes, ogsaa efter at den er sendt. En
    faktura baerer sin egen kopi af kunden, taget da den blev dannet, og den kopi
    var laast sammen med belob og linjer. Var adressen tastet forkert, kunne
    fakturaen derfor aldrig naa kunden: at rette kundekortet hjalp ikke, for
    fakturaen laeser sin egen kopi, og den eneste vej uden om var at taste
    adressen ind i haanden i sende-dialogen hver eneste gang. Nu rettes den paa
    fakturaen, og aendringen staar i fakturaens forlob med foer og efter. Belob,
    linjer, navn og fakturaadresse er fortsat laaste – det er hele grunden til at
    en sendt faktura er laast.

1.37.54

  • 1.37.53 tog hele sitet ned, hvis Pro var aeldre end Free. AuditTrail fik en
    paakraevet fjerde parameter, men Pro booter sin egen kopi af den klasse og
    kaldte fortsat med tre. Parameteren er nu valgfri, saa en aeldre Pro ikke
    kan vaelte Free igen.

1.37.53

  • Loggen skrev “AEndrede opgave” uden at sige hvilken. Navnet paa det beroerte
    element gemmes nu, naar handlingen sker – opgavenummer, titel og kunde – og
    vises i loggen. At slaa det op bagefter ville efterlade netop sletningerne
    uden navn, for der findes raekken ikke mere.
  • Slettes en henvendelse, en kunde eller en opgave helt, staar det nu i loggen
    med navnet paa det, der blev slettet.
  • Over halvdelen af loggen var brugerflade-husholdning: markering af badges som
    set, aabning af dagens overblik, laesning af notifikationer. Det logges ikke
    laengere. Kun handlinger paa forretningsdata.
  • Titler og emner ligger krypteret og blev aldrig sammenlignet, saa loggen
    kunne kun sige at titlen “blev angivet”. De laeses nu, saa aendringen staar
    med foer og efter.
  • Feltnavne blev filtreret bort, hvis de lignede noget personfoelsomt, saa en
    aendret adresse forsvandt helt ud af loggen. Navnet paa et felt er ikke det
    foelsomme – vaerdien er. Navnene staar nu altid, mens vaerdierne for
    personoplysninger fortsat holdes ude.
  • Loggens taeller svarede 0, mens listen leverede en fuld side, saa Forrige og
    Naeste aldrig kunne virke. Taellingen stiller nu samme spoergsmaal som listen.

1.37.52

  • En opgave kan nu holde flere tilsyn. Hvert tilsyn har titel, status,
    planlagt og udfoert tidspunkt, varighed, hvem der var der og en
    bemaerkning, og de staar som en liste paa opgaven. Foer dette var den
    eneste maade at notere to tilsyn paa at skrive det i opgavens titel, hvor
    ingen optaelling eller sum kunne laese det.
  • Registreret tid paa en opgave er nu summen af de tilsyn, der er markeret
    udfoert, og vedligeholdes automatisk. Opgaver uden tilsyn beholder det tal,
    der er skrevet i haanden.
  • Loggen blev tegnet tom for brugere, der har Lead to Cash-rettighederne,
    men ikke ogsaa er WordPress-administratorer. Menupunktet blev vist ud fra
    den rettighed, serveren faktisk kraever, mens indlaesningen spurgte efter
    WordPress’ manage_options og derfor aldrig sendte forespoergslen. Siden saa
    tom ud uden fejlbesked, mens raekkerne laa urorte i databasen. Begge steder
    bruger nu samme port som serveren.

1.37.51

  • Aendringsloggen i readme.txt stoppede ved 1.37.29, og det er den, der vises
    paa plugin-siden hos wordpress.org. Enogtyve udgivelser var dermed usynlige
    for alle, der ikke havde pakken i forvejen. Posterne fra 1.37.30 og frem er
    nu skrevet ind, saa siden viser det samme som changelog.txt.
  • Ingen aendringer i kode eller funktion.

1.37.50

  • Opretter man en kunde direkte, bliver der nu spurgt, om der skal laves en
    henvendelse paa kunden. Svarer man ja, aabner henvendelsen med kunden
    udfyldt. Det er ikke et krav – flytter man et bestaaende kundekartotek ind,
    er svaret nej hver gang, og et krav ville spaerre for det.
  • Kunder uden en henvendelse er maerket “Ingen henvendelse” ved navnet i
    kundelisten. Foer stod der et nul i henvendelseskolonnen, som var let at
    overse, og i Pro stod der ingenting. Uden en henvendelse er der intet at
    haenge en pris, en opgave eller en faktura paa, og kunden staar uden for
    henvendelsestallene.

1.37.49

  • En faktura, der naevner sin egen opgave, lukkede ogsaa kundens andre opgaver
    paa samme henvendelse. En kunde her har en vaskehal og et salgskontor paa
    samme henvendelse; regningen for salgskontoret fik vaskehallens 43.250 kr.
    til at forsvinde ud af baade kundekolonnen og “Samlet opgavevaerdi”. Kun
    bilag uden egen opgave lukker nu en opgave paa henvendelsen – naevner
    bilaget en opgave, har det betalt for den opgave, ikke for de andre.
  • Kontakter, der er sat til at blive holdt ude af tallene, taelles ikke
    laengere med i summerne paa kundeoversigten. Tre proevefakturaer paa en
    krone fik “Faktureret netto” til at staa 3,00 kr. over rapportens tal.
    Raekken viser fortsat sit eget beloeb; det er summen, flaget handler om.

1.37.48

  • Afslutter man en kunde, der stadig har en aaben opgave, bliver der nu
    spurgt foerst, og opgavens nummer og titel staar i spoergsmaalet. Opgaven
    forsvinder ikke af at kunden lukkes – den holder bare op med at ligge
    oeverst, og dens budget bliver ved at staa i tallene som arbejde, der
    venter paa en regning.
  • Ikke en spaerring: svarer man ja, afsluttes kunden. Afslaget kommer fra
    serveren, saa det gaelder ogsaa et API-kald, ikke kun listen.

1.37.47

  • “Samlet opgaveværdi” lagde det fakturerede sammen med alle prissatte
    opgaver, men udelukkede kun en opgave, hvis fakturaen pegede direkte paa
    den. De fleste bilag peger paa henvendelsen i stedet, saa betalt arbejde
    blev talt med baade som faktureret og som forventet – paa denne
    installation 16.000 kr. for meget.
  • Tallet regnes nu samme sted som kundelistens kolonne: opgavebudget hvor der
    ikke er faktureret, ellers estimatet paa henvendelsen, aldrig to kilder paa
    samme henvendelse. Estimaterne er dermed med, hvor de foer manglede helt.
  • job_expected_ex_vat_minor staar uroert for dem, der laeser det; det nye tal
    hedder uninvoiced_value_ex_vat_minor.

1.37.46

  • “Estimeret, ikke faktureret” kunne staa ved siden af et beloeb, der allerede
    var faktureret. Udelukkelsen spurgte kun, om fakturaen bar henvendelsens id,
    men de fleste bilag goer ikke – de henfoeres via opgaven eller via kundens
    senest vundne henvendelse foer bilaget. En faktureret henvendelse saa derfor
    ufaktureret ud, og dens estimat blev talt med oveni. Samme arbejde to gange.
  • Udelukkelsen bruger nu samme tre trin som rapporten, gennem den faelles
    LeadAttribution, saa der kun er ét sted at rette reglen.

1.37.45

  • “Estimeret, ikke faktureret” talte kun budgetter paa opgaver. En kunde med
    41.907 kr. i estimat paa selve henvendelsen og ingen opgave stod derfor
    stadig med 0,00 kr., mens kundekortet viste estimatet lige nedenunder. To
    skaerme, samme kunde, to svar.
  • Vaerdien tages nu fra den bedste kilde henvendelsen har, i samme raekkefoelge
    som rapporten bruger: er der faktureret, taeller intet her; ellers
    opgavebudgettet; ellers estimatet paa henvendelsen. Aldrig to af dem paa
    samme henvendelse – et estimat og et opgavebudget er to gaet paa det samme
    arbejde, ikke to stykker arbejde.

1.37.44

  • Kundeoversigten viser nu ogsaa totalerne “Faktureret netto” og “Estimeret,
    ikke faktureret” ved siden af udestaaende. De tre svarer paa hver sit
    spoergsmaal om de samme kunder – hvad der er sendt regning paa, hvad der
    ligger paa opgaverne uden at vaere faktureret, og hvad der mangler at blive
    betalt – og hver for sig er de til at misforstaa.

1.37.43

  • Kundeoversigten viser nu ogsaa “Estimeret, ikke faktureret”. En kunde med en
    opgave til 20.000 kr. stod med 0,00 kr. i begge beloebskolonner, og begge tal
    var rigtige – der var ikke faktureret noget, og der skyldtes derfor heller
    ikke noget – men listen saa ud, som om der slet ikke laa arbejde paa kunden.
  • Beloebet er budgettet paa opgaven, ikke en pris kunden har accepteret. Derfor
    hedder kolonnen “estimeret” og ikke “aftalt”.
  • En opgave taelles kun med, hvis hverken den selv eller dens henvendelse har
    en faktura. Fakturaen haenger ikke altid paa opgaven, og uden den regel ville
    en opgave til 10.000 med 6.000 faktureret staa med hele sit budget ved siden
    af de 6.000 i fakturerings-kolonnen – det samme arbejde talt to gange.
    Reglen underdriver hellere end at puste op.

1.37.42

  • Kolonneoverskriften “Faktureret netto” stod paa engelsk i en dansk
    brugerflade. Overskrifterne oversaettes gennem i18n, og den nye stod ikke paa
    listen – saa den faldt tilbage til sin engelske kildetekst og var den eneste
    engelske overskrift i tabellen.

1.37.41

  • Et bilag henfoeres ikke laengere til en henvendelse, der foerst blev vundet
    bagefter. Reglen satte sit svar til kundens aeldste vundne henvendelse, foer
    den begyndte at lede, og var alle vundet efter bilaget, blev den foerste
    returneret alligevel – en faktura fra marts kunne saaledes staa paa en
    henvendelse vundet i maj. Omsaetningen forsvandt ikke, men den laa paa det
    forkerte arbejde. Nu vaelges intet, naar intet var vundet i tide, og bilaget
    taelles som ikke henfoert, hvor det kan ses.
  • Kundeoversigten viser nu “Faktureret netto” ved siden af udestaaende. De to
    er blevet forvekslet, og det er til at forstaa: en kunde med en betalt
    faktura paa 20.000 stod med 0,00 kr., fordi 0 var det rigtige svar paa et
    andet spoergsmaal. Beloebet er uden moms, kreditnotaer traekker fra, og hvert
    bilag taelles én gang. Kilden er den samme tabel som udestaaende regnes af.
  • Rapporten har faaet fem vaerdikategorier, der udelukker hinanden og summerer
    til de vundne henvendelser: faktureret, aftalt men ikke faktureret, kun
    estimat, og uden registreret vaerdi – med delvist faktureret som en
    delmaengde af faktureret, ikke en kategori for sig. Et estimat regnes aldrig
    som en accepteret ordre. De hidtidige felter staar uroert ved siden af.
  • Diagnosen taeller nu ogsaa de bilag, rapporten aldrig ser: fakturaer til en
    kunde uden en eneste vundet henvendelse, og fuldt krediterede par. Begge dele
    hoerer med rette udenfor, men en sum, der udelader noget uden at sige det, er
    svaer at afstemme mod regnskabet.

1.37.40

  • Ny read-only diagnose af hvordan en vundet henvendelse fik sin vaerdi.
    Rapporten kunne sige “elleve henvendelser uden kendt vaerdi”, men ikke
    hvilke elleve, hvad der blev ledt efter, eller hvorfor der intet blev
    fundet – og saa kunne tallet ikke efterproeves af andre end den, der
    ville laese forespoergslerne igennem. Ruten svarer paa netop det: pr.
    henvendelse vaerdikilden og aarsagen, pr. bilag hvilken henvendelse det
    blev henfoert til, ved hvilken af de tre metoder, og om valget var
    rettidigt. Den skriver intet, hverken her eller i regnskabet.
  • Adgangen er rapportens egen, og en begraenset konsulent afvises af selve
    ruten – at skjule et menupunkt er ingen adgangskontrol. Svaret indeholder
    public id’er, datoer, beloeb og metoder, og hverken navne, e-mail,
    telefon eller adresser.
  • Reglen for hvilken henvendelse et bilag hoerer til er flyttet fra
    rapporten ud i en faelles service, saa diagnosen og rapporten svarer det
    samme. To kopier ville foer eller siden give to svar paa det samme
    spoergsmaal. Flytningen aendrer ingen tal: den er ordret, og en proeve
    haandhaever det.

1.37.39

  • En kreditnota er ikke en faktura, der venter paa penge. Fakturalisten talte
    kreditnotaerne med blandt de sendte: tre af dem fik “Sendt” til at staa paa
    fem, mens to fakturaer faktisk var ude. En krediteret faktura havde laenge
    haft sin egen rubrik, men selve kreditnotaen faldt igennem til sin
    almindelige status – og en kreditnota er “sendt” som ethvert andet dokument.
    Den har nu sin egen taelling, saa fliserne stadig svarer til raekkerne i
    listen. Beloebene var rigtige i forvejen; de modregnede parret.

1.37.37

  • Ny status Ikke relevant. Manden der troede vi var kommunen, henvendelsen
    fra den anden ende af landet, leverandoeren der ringede paa salgsnummeret –
    de skal modtages og besvares som alt andet, men at arkivere dem som “Tabt”
    siger, at vi bod paa arbejdet og tabte. Det traekker vindprocenten ned for
    arbejde, ingen nogensinde har haft. Den nye status lukker henvendelsen –
    ingen opfoelgning, ikke “aaben” – og holdes ude af salgstallene.
  • Henvendelser taget af en maskine taeller foerst med, naar et menneske har
    set paa dem. En AI-telefonbesked er et gaet paa hvad opkaldet handlede om,
    og et gaet hoerer ikke hjemme i en konverteringsrate. Den staar ude af
    salgstallene saa laenge status er “Ny”, og taeller fra det oejeblik nogen
    giver den en rigtig status – i den uge opkaldet kom, for det var da
    telefonen ringede.
  • Og den mekanisme virkede slet ikke foer. Lead to …

short_description: Manage enquiries, customers, quotes, jobs, invoices and reports in a self-hosted WordPress workflow.
description:
Lead to Cash by NimblePlugins is a self-hosted workflow for service businesses that want to manage the path from enquiry to invoice inside WordPress.

Most small service businesses run on a contact form, a spreadsheet, a folder of PDF files and an accounting program that first hears about a job once it is over. Lead to Cash replaces the middle of that chain. An enquiry arrives, becomes a quote, the quote becomes a job, the job becomes an invoice, and the invoice is followed until it is paid – in one place, on your own server, with the history of every step kept beside the record it belongs to.

It is not a set of custom post types with an admin screen in front. Lead to Cash creates its own database tables and runs as a private single-page app on your site, opened from the WordPress admin menu and reachable only by the users you give access to. The working day happens in that app; the WordPress admin is where you configure it.

From enquiry to paid invoice

Enquiries. New enquiries are listed as they arrive, with the source they came from, the owner responsible, the status, and the next action with a date on it. Actions whose date has passed are raised on the dashboard before you start, so nothing waits quietly. Enquiries that come in by phone are written straight into the same list, and a second enquiry on a contact who already has one open is flagged before it is saved.

Customers. Each contact has a single record: details, the enquiries behind them, their documents, what they currently owe, and the activity history beside it. A Danish CVR number or a European VAT number can be looked up, so the registered name and address are filled in for you.

Quotes. A quote is written with line items, an introduction and your own terms attached, produced as a PDF and emailed to the customer from the site. Every quote carries its value and its expiry date, so the pipeline shows what is genuinely still open rather than everything ever sent.

Jobs. An accepted quote becomes a job with an owner, a deadline, a priority and an economy of its own. Finished work moves to a completed list that stays searchable, with the invoices raised against it linked from the job.

Invoices. Invoices are produced as PDF documents with your payment terms and, if you use one, a payment QR code. An invoice runs from draft to paid and keeps track of partial payments, credit notes and what is overdue – and it remembers which job it came from.

Reports and audit log. The reports cover enquiries received, win rate, what was quoted, what was invoiced, what was paid, and how long payment actually took. The audit log records every change: who made it, when, and what it touched.

What the free plugin includes

  • Enquiries and manual lead creation
  • Customers
  • Quotes and PDF documents
  • Jobs and completed work
  • Invoices and payment tracking
  • Standard reports and an audit log
  • In-app notifications
  • Search and export tools
  • Local encryption of sensitive fields
  • WordPress personal-data export and erasure integration
  • English as the default product language
  • Danish language and economic defaults
  • A searchable Help & FAQ centre in English and Danish
  • Lead to Cash user administration in WordPress
  • Scheduled backups of Lead to Cash data, kept on the server, with restore and import of a saved backup file

Users and access

Whether a person may open Lead to Cash at all is a WordPress capability, carried by a dedicated “Lead to Cash operator” role that the plugin adds. What they may do once inside is a separate setting with three levels – User, Consultant and Admin – so an administrator of the website is not automatically an administrator of the business data. Both are managed from the WordPress admin.

Your data stays on your server

Lead to Cash stores everything in its own tables in your WordPress database, and keeps its backups there as well. Sensitive contact and activity fields are encrypted locally with an installation key that is never sent anywhere, and you can define that key in wp-config.php so that a copy of the database on its own cannot decrypt your customer data.

The plugin never contacts NimblePlugins, sends no analytics and has no telemetry. It reaches the internet only when a user asks for something that needs it – a CVR or VAT lookup, or a logo or QR image given as a web address. Each case is listed under External services below.

It also plugs into WordPress’s own Export Personal Data and Erase Personal Data tools, and it can remove every trace of itself on uninstall if you turn that option on.

English and Danish

English is the product language. Danish is translated throughout, and choosing it also switches the economic defaults: DKK, 25% VAT, CVR labels and Danish document prefixes. Documents that are already saved keep the values they were written with. A searchable Help & FAQ centre is built in, in both languages.

No licence, no account, no time limit

The free plugin is complete on its own. There is no licence check, no account requirement, no feature that expires and no upsell in the middle of the workflow. A product key applies only to the separately installed Lead to Cash Pro add-on, whose code is not part of this plugin.

Product information: https://nimbleplugins.com/lead-to-cash/

External services

Lead to Cash runs on your own server and never contacts NimblePlugins. It contacts the services below, and only for the feature named.

Danish company register, CVR (only when a user looks up a CVR number)

When a user enters a Danish CVR number on a customer card and asks for the details, the eight-digit number is sent to cvrapi.dk to fetch the registered company name and address. The request also carries this site’s host name in the User-Agent header, because cvrapi.dk rejects anonymous calls. Nothing else is sent, and no customer data leaves the site. An answer is cached for twelve hours, so looking the same number up again does not call out again.

Service: https://cvrapi.dk/ – Terms: https://cvrapi.dk/terms – What data they hold and why: https://cvrapi.dk/help

VAT-number lookup (only when a user clicks it)

When a user looks up a customer’s VAT number, the country code and the number are sent to the European Commission’s VIES service (ec.europa.eu) to fetch the registered company name and address. Nothing else is sent. Service: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/ – Legal notice: https://commission.europa.eu/legal-notice_en – Privacy: https://commission.europa.eu/privacy-policy-websites-managed-european-commission_en

Logo and payment QR image

If the company logo or payment QR code is given as a web address, Lead to Cash downloads that image to place it in PDF documents. Only the address you enter is requested, and nothing about your data is sent. Normally this is an image in your own media library.

Backup destinations (only with the separate Pro add-on)

Lead to Cash takes backups and keeps them on this server. Sending a copy somewhere else is what Pro adds: Pro registers the destinations, and without Pro there are none, so a backup stays where it was made.

This package does contain the Dropbox client class, because Pro builds on it rather than carrying its own copy. It is never reached without Pro: every path to it runs through a destination, and no destination exists until Pro registers one.

With Pro installed and a destination configured, the backup archive is uploaded to the destination you chose, each time a backup runs. The archive contains all Lead to Cash data, so choose a destination you would trust with the database itself.

Dropbox: https://www.dropbox.com/ – Terms: https://www.dropbox.com/terms – Privacy: https://www.dropbox.com/privacy

Google Drive: https://www.google.com/drive/ – Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms – Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

OneDrive and SharePoint: https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/onedrive – Terms: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement – Privacy: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/privacy/privacystatement

SFTP and webhook destinations go to an address you enter yourself; no third party is involved beyond the one you choose.

Source code

Lead to Cash has no build step. The JavaScript and CSS shipped in frontend/ and admin/ are the source: written by hand, not generated, bundled or minified, and they are the same files the browser loads. There is nothing to un-minify, and there are no build tools to document.

Privacy

Lead to Cash stores contact details, enquiry details, notes, document data and activity history in the local WordPress database. Sensitive fields are encrypted locally.

The plugin integrates with WordPress personal-data export and erasure tools. Site administrators remain responsible for defining suitable retention periods. Financial records may need to be retained under applicable bookkeeping rules.

Lead to Cash does not contact NimblePlugins. Backups sent to a destination contain all Lead to Cash data; choose a destination you would trust with the database itself.

1.37.29

  • Tabellen til udgaaende beskeder bliver nu faktisk oprettet naar en
    eksisterende installation opdaterer. Tabellen kom med i 1.37.28, men
    skemaversionen blev staaende paa 0.9.2, og opgraderingen koerer kun
    skematrinnet naar den vaerdi aendrer sig. En ny installation fik tabellen,
    en opdateret gjorde ikke – og fejlen kunne kun ses paa et site der havde
    pluginnet i forvejen.

1.37.28

  • Henvendelser tælles nu på hvornår de kom ind, ikke på hvornår de blev
    skrevet ned. En henvendelse fra juli, der først tastes ind i oktober,
    hørte til oktober i rapporten – så juli mistede den, og oktober fik en
    for meget. Feltet “Modtaget” på henvendelsen afgør det, og rapporten,
    ugetællingen og begge lister regner nu på det samme.

1.37.25

  • Gennemført én regel i rapporten: det realiserede vinder altid. Er der
    først en faktura på en opgave eller en henvendelse, ER fakturaen værdien,
    og budgettet eller det aftalte beløb tæller ikke med nogen steder – hverken
    som rest eller som et højere tal.
  • Restbeløbet på delvist fakturerede opgaver er fjernet helt.
  • “Gns. hvor værdien er kendt” tog før det største af det fakturerede og det
    aftalte. Et budget, ingen nogensinde fakturerede, kunne dermed slå den
    faktura, der afsluttede sagen. Nu er det fakturaen, når der er en.
  • “Aftalt, endnu ikke faktureret” dækker nu kun sager helt uden faktura.

1.37.24

  • Noterne under Samlet opgaveværdi er fjernet. Opdelingen står allerede på
    siden, og tre linjer under et tal gør kortet sværere at læse, ikke lettere.

1.37.23

  • Henvendelsesraten talte forud. Med en periode, der løb til 31. december,
    blev november og december regnet med som stille måneder, og raten blev
    delt med tid, der ikke var gået: 48 henvendelser blev til 9,1 om måneden
    i stedet for 18,7. Den regner nu frem til i dag, som ugelisten altid har
    gjort.

1.37.22

  • Rapporter målte værdi på henvendelser. En henvendelse er ikke en værdi, og
    en kunde er det heller ikke – værdien opstår først, når nogen skriver ned,
    hvad en opgave koster. Kortet hedder nu “Samlet opgaveværdi” og er det
    fakturerede plus budgettet på de opgaver, der endnu ikke er faktureret.
  • Er en opgave budgetteret højere, end den er faktureret, står forskellen
    frem som aftalt, ikke endnu faktureret arbejde. Før forsvandt den helt.
  • Rapportperioden starter som hele indeværende år, 1. januar til 31. december,
    i stedet for et vindue, der gled en dag frem hver morgen.

1.37.21

  • Statusfilteret “Alle” på opgavelisten skjulte de afsluttede. Det modsagde sit
    eget navn, og en afsluttet opgave kunne kun ses i den separate
    Afsluttede-visning. “Alle” betyder nu alle.
  • “Planlagt” er valgt som standard, for det er den liste, man handler på.

1.37.20

  • Opgaver kunne blive til tvillinger. Gemmestien afgjorde opret-eller-opdatér
    ud fra et data-attribut på formularen, som blev nulstillet, hver gang
    dialogen blev lukket. En formular, der havde mistet sit id, oprettede derfor
    en ny opgave i stedet for at gemme den, der stod på skærmen. Identiteten
    læses nu af selve posten; attributtet er kun et krydstjek.
  • Opretter du en opgave på en kunde, der allerede har en åben, viser appen de
    eksisterende og spørger, før den opretter. Serveren afviser en ubekræftet
    dublet og sender de åbne opgaver med tilbage, så spørgsmålet kan nævne dem.
    Det er et spørgsmål, ikke et forbud — to åbne opgaver på samme kunde er ofte
    rigtigt.
  • Nøgletallet på opgavelisten var ét tal, der lagde fakturerede beløb sammen
    med håndtastede budgetter, og som talte alle opgaver med — også de
    afsluttede, tabellen ikke viser. Samme arbejde kunne derfor tælle to gange:
    én gang som omsætning på den afsluttede opgave, én gang som forventning på
    tvillingen. Det er nu to tal — Faktureret og Forventet — og begge følger det,
    der står i listen, så filter og søgning virker på dem.
  • Økonomikolonnen blandede momsgrundlag: fakturerede opgaver viste beløb
    inklusive moms, resten viste budget uden. Alt vises nu ekskl. moms, og det
    står i kolonneoverskriften.

1.37.19

  • Appens adresse kan nu vælges. Har sitet allerede en side på /lead-to-cash/ —
    en produktside, en landingsside — nægtede pluginnet at blive aktiveret, og
    eneste udvej var at omdøbe den eksisterende side. Det er ikke rimeligt at
    forlange af et site, der havde adressen først. Sæt
    define( ‘NIMBLE_LTC_APP_SLUG’, ‘din-slug’ ); i wp-config.php før
    aktivering, så bruger appen den i stedet. Pro henter PWA’ens id, start_url,
    scope og Service-Worker-Allowed fra samme konstant, så det følger med.
  • Fejlbeskeden ved adressekonflikt sagde ikke, hvad man skulle gøre, og skrev
    altid “/lead-to-cash/” selv hvis appen lå et andet sted. Den viser nu den
    rigtige adresse og nævner konstanten.
  • Bemærk: ændrer man adressen på en eksisterende installation, skal
    permalinks gemmes igen, og PWA’en skifter scope, så genveje må tilføjes
    forfra.

1.37.18

  • Kundekortets overskrift stacker nu ordentligt på telefon. Henvisningen “Også
    kunde som …” klemte sig ind ved siden af navnet, wrappede over tre linjer og
    maste lukkekrydset. Navn og kryds beholder den første række, og henvisningen
    får en række for sig selv nedenunder. Et langt kundenavn kan ikke længere

1.37.17

    almindelige knapstil — præcis den blå, den ikke måtte være. Farverne står nu
    direkte, med en mørk guld til lyst tema og en lys til mørkt.
